categories.name: Inform
categories.definition: Mitigations that work by changing what is known or believed about AI.

categories.name: Research & Evidence
categories.definition: Mitigations involving the generation and dissemination of new knowledge and evidence.
categories.scope: Studies, data collection, research resources and tools, datasets, shared research infrastructure.
categories.exclusions: Instruments involving testing → Evaluation. Dissemination as training/education/literacy → Training domain. Non-research reporting → Disclosure.
categories.key_examples: Research studies; Research datasets; Foresight/horizon scanning

categories.name: Information Sharing & Disclosure
categories.definition: Mitigations involving the open communication and sharing of information across actors.
categories.scope: Disclosure, reporting, notification, and information sharing across actors.
categories.exclusions: Generation of new knowledge or evidence → Research. Creation of a rule requiring disclosure → Standards/Law/Policies.
categories.key_examples: Disclosure and reporting of incidents; Information sharing on industry registries

categories.name: Govern
categories.definition: Mitigations that work by changing the rules that AI actors are expected to follow.

categories.name: Law & Regulation
categories.definition: Mitigations involving the creation or adoption of systematic rules by an external authority with jurisdiction over the target.
categories.scope: Statute, legislature, court rulings, contracts, liability regimes.
categories.key_examples: EU AI Act; Export controls on AI chips; Statutory requirement to conduct risk assessments

categories.name: External Standards
categories.definition: Mitigations involving the creation and adoption of shared systematic rules from a peer or industry body (external, voluntary).
categories.scope: Industry standards, codes of practice, shared frameworks.
categories.exclusions: Evaluating/auditing/certifying against a standard → Evaluation. A standard mandated by regulation stays here, but the mandating regulation → Law. Co-regulation or government-endorsed → Law. Rules an actor authors for itself → Policies. Built controls → Technical. Contracts → Law.
categories.key_examples: NIST AI RMF; OECD AI principles; Industry safety pledges

categories.name: Internal Policies
categories.definition: Mitigations involving the creation and adoption of systematic rules by an actor for itself, internally, including for its own staff.
categories.scope: Internal policies, public commitments, named plans and frameworks authored by the actor.
categories.exclusions: Vague, one-off, generic, or unnamed rules → Practices. Operational workflows that are not named rules → Practices. Shared rules from a peer/industry body → Standards.
categories.key_examples: Internal responsible-AI policy; A named safety framework the org authors

categories.name: Implement
categories.definition: Mitigations that work by directly changing what is done to and around AI systems in practice.

categories.name: Technical Artifacts
categories.definition: Mitigations that are built into the AI system or its supporting infrastructure.
categories.scope: Technical tools, innovations, systems, architecture, interfaces, and environments.

categories.name: Practices & Processes
categories.definition: Mitigations consisting of procedures, workflows, or ways of working that humans carry out.
categories.exclusions: A well-defined rule or policy an actor authors or adopts → Standards/Law/Policies. Continuous observation to surface problems → Monitoring.
categories.key_examples: Incident-response procedures; Review and sign-off workflows; Pre-deployment checklists

categories.name: Monitoring
categories.definition: Mitigations consisting of the continuous observation of an AI system, its behaviour, use, or effects to surface problems on an ongoing basis.
categories.scope: Ongoing, continuous observation; logging; drift and anomaly detection.
categories.exclusions: Organizational reporting externally → Disclosure. A one-off procedure → Practices. A built monitor is Monitoring by function, not Technical. A discrete evaluative act → Evaluation.
categories.key_examples: Run-time behaviour monitoring; Logging/audit trails; Drift detection

categories.name: Evaluation & Audit
categories.definition: Mitigations that primarily involve testing or checking against a standard or expectation; a discrete evaluative act producing an assessment.
categories.exclusions: Automatic runtime conditionals → Technical. The creation of a standard or framework → Standards. A catalogue of controls is Standards/Policies until it is implemented. Continuous ongoing observation → Monitoring. Knowledge generation with no criterion → Research.
categories.key_examples: Testing a model against benchmarks; Third-party audits; Dangerous-capability evaluations

categories.name: Other
categories.definition: Mitigations whose instrument does not fit in the above modalities or which are unclassifiable for other reasons.

categories.name: Other (Additional)
categories.definition: Clear instruments not captured above (e.g., training/education, advocacy, market mechanisms — levers that are folded into the domain axis; tag the instrument here).

categories.name: Other (Cross-cutting)
categories.definition: Instruments that are broad, ambiguous, a combination, or cross-cutting across modalities, or otherwise cannot be confidently classified.
